world.title: South Africa’s ANC falls to 30.76% in historic local election defeat
world.summary: South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC), which has governed since the end of apartheid, won 30.76% of the vote in municipal elections held Nov. 4, its worst result on record. The Democratic Alliance (DA), the main opposition party, took 24.64%. The ANC remained the largest party nationally but lost its majority
world.content: South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC), which has governed since the end of apartheid, won 30.76% of the vote in municipal elections held Nov. 4, its worst result on record. The Democratic Alliance (DA), the main opposition party, took 24.64%. The ANC remained the largest party nationally but lost its majority in six of the country’s eight metropolitan areas, leaving parties to negotiate control of many councils. The ANC lost support over repeated water shortages and electricity outages, deteriorating roads and other municipal service failures, as well as corruption, unemployment and crime. ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula acknowledged that communities had gone without water and refuse collection and that roads had not been maintained. More than half of the 213 municipal councils had no outright majority, and parties have 14 days to negotiate coalitions and form local administrations. The DA retained its majority in Cape Town; the ANC’s reduced support leaves it dependent on partners in cities where it once governed alone.
world.image_alt: South Africa’s ANC falls to 30.76% in historic local election defeat

world.title: 200,000 march in Amsterdam pressing Dutch government on Israel
world.summary: About 200,000 people marched through Amsterdam on Sunday, according to organizers, urging the Dutch government to impose tougher trade sanctions on Israel, stop arms sales and formally describe Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide. Many wore red and carried Palestinian flags and signs. Israel rejects the genocide accus
world.content: About 200,000 people marched through Amsterdam on Sunday, according to organizers, urging the Dutch government to impose tougher trade sanctions on Israel, stop arms sales and formally describe Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide. Many wore red and carried Palestinian flags and signs. Israel rejects the genocide accusation. The fourth “Red Line” demonstration called for stronger Dutch action as attacks and severe humanitarian needs continue in Gaza despite a ceasefire that began in October 2025. Gaza’s Health Ministry says Israeli forces have killed more than 1,550 Palestinians since the ceasefire began. The ministry does not distinguish civilians from combatants and says women and children account for roughly half of the dead. Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who did not attend, said Friday his government was increasing diplomatic pressure on Israel and pressing Hamas over actions threatening Israeli civilians. The rally followed a Dutch ban on imports from Israeli settlements, which prompted Israel to revoke Dutch diplomats’ accreditation.
world.image_alt: 200,000 march in Amsterdam pressing Dutch government on Israel

world.title: Europe secures place in US-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
world.summary: France says European representatives will join U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, expanding what had been described as a three-way format. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot did not identify who would represent France or clarify whether European officials would negotiate di
world.content: France says European representatives will join U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, expanding what had been described as a three-way format. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot did not identify who would represent France or clarify whether European officials would negotiate directly or observe. The meeting is the first round of talks since February. The agenda includes Ukraine’s postwar security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues. Russia wants Ukraine to withdraw from four regions Moscow claims to have annexed and abandon its bid to join NATO; Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects ceding territory and says any security guarantees must specify how partners would respond to another Russian attack. Moscow had objected to European participation, while Washington says it will consult European partners and could expand the talks if they make progress. U.S. President Donald Trump has referred to a possible agreement involving Europe, but U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no plan has been finalized. The talks follow a Brussels meeting of U.S., European, Ukrainian and NATO officials last Thursday.
world.image_alt: Europe secures place in US-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi

world.title: Houthi attack damages Aramco tower as missiles target Riyadh
world.summary: Yemen’s Houthi movement said it launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia on Sunday. Falling debris damaged a Saudi Aramco administrative tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District. Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry reported minor damage and no injuries or deaths; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted mis
world.content: Yemen’s Houthi movement said it launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia on Sunday. Falling debris damaged a Saudi Aramco administrative tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District. Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry reported minor damage and no injuries or deaths; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and other areas. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the operation also targeted King Khalid International Airport, Aramco oil storage and facilities in Abqaiq. The attack followed Saudi-led airstrikes near Sanaa on Saturday. Houthi-run health authorities said at least 33 people were killed and 39 wounded; the figures and responsibility for the strikes have not been independently verified. The Houthis described their attacks on Saudi Arabia as retaliation. The coalition said it later destroyed two missile launchers in Yemen’s Saada province that it said were used in the Riyadh attack. Fighting resumed in July after a 2022 truce collapsed. Since then, the Houthis have expanded attacks on Saudi airports, ports and energy infrastructure, while Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes in Yemen. The United Nations has reported more than 1,600 deaths and the displacement of over 300,000 people since the renewed fighting began.
world.image_alt: Houthi attack damages Aramco tower as missiles target Riyadh

world.title: Senegal migrant boat sinking kills at least 35, search continues
world.summary: At least 35 people died and one survived when a migrant boat sank off northwestern Senegal, emergency services said Sunday night. Search teams were still looking for an unknown number of missing people. The boat went down near Loumpoul in the Kébémer department; officials have not said how many people were aboard. The
world.content: At least 35 people died and one survived when a migrant boat sank off northwestern Senegal, emergency services said Sunday night. Search teams were still looking for an unknown number of missing people. The boat went down near Loumpoul in the Kébémer department; officials have not said how many people were aboard. The death toll rose from 21 on Saturday to at least 35 on Sunday. The boat was carrying people seeking to migrate irregularly along the Atlantic route from West Africa toward Spain’s Canary Islands. The Spanish migrant-rights group Walking Borders counted at least 635 deaths on the route in the first five months of 2026 and estimated that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the islands. Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye pledged to pursue those organizing the crossings. The interior minister is due to visit the area on Monday, Nov. 9, as search operations continue.
world.image_alt: Senegal migrant boat sinking kills at least 35, search continues

world.title: UN climate talks open in Turkey as energy crisis tests pledges
world.summary: The United Nations’ COP31 climate negotiations opened Monday in Antalya, Turkey, with representatives from nearly 200 countries scheduled to meet through Nov. 20 to discuss implementing climate commitments, climate finance and the transition from fossil fuels. Turkey holds the conference presidency, while Australian Cl
world.content: The United Nations’ COP31 climate negotiations opened Monday in Antalya, Turkey, with representatives from nearly 200 countries scheduled to meet through Nov. 20 to discuss implementing climate commitments, climate finance and the transition from fossil fuels. Turkey holds the conference presidency, while Australian Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen leads negotiations under an arrangement reached after the two countries disputed hosting rights. The talks open with war disrupting oil supplies, artificial intelligence driving up power demand and the Trump administration staying away. Turkey is proposing a nonbinding target to increase electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from about one-fifth to 35% by 2035. Climate advocates say the proposal does not ensure that new electricity comes from low-carbon sources. A coalition including vulnerable Pacific island countries is seeking a clearer roadmap away from fossil fuels, while oil- and gas-producing countries including Saudi Arabia argue that fossil fuels can remain in the energy mix if emissions are reduced or captured. Negotiators also face a dispute over support for poorer countries: developing nations are estimated to need $305 billion a year for adaptation by 2035, compared with $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in international public adaptation finance in 2024. A World Leaders’ Summit is scheduled for Nov. 11-12, and the negotiations are due to conclude Nov. 20.
world.image_alt: UN climate talks open in Turkey as energy crisis tests pledges

world.title: Krakow gunman dies as terror investigation examines nine deaths
world.summary: A 24-year-old Polish man suspected of killing six people in Krakow’s Main Market Square died in hospital Monday, two days after police shot him during the attack, authorities said. Prosecutors are investigating the Saturday shooting as a terrorist offence and examining whether the suspect also killed his parents and si
world.content: A 24-year-old Polish man suspected of killing six people in Krakow’s Main Market Square died in hospital Monday, two days after police shot him during the attack, authorities said. Prosecutors are investigating the Saturday shooting as a terrorist offence and examining whether the suspect also killed his parents and sister, whose bodies were found at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. The six victims were four Polish citizens, a British man and an Austrian woman; 15 other people were wounded, including two police officers and five foreign nationals. Officers confronted the gunman within minutes. Two surgeons who were nearby began treating the wounded before ambulances arrived, and one doctor’s colleague helped stem a critically injured officer’s bleeding. Poland’s two days of national mourning began Sunday and continued Monday, while Krakow’s square reopened to the public as mourners placed candles and flowers there. Investigators are still examining the suspect’s possible far-right influences and the circumstances of the three deaths at his family home; officials have not established a motive.
world.image_alt: Krakow gunman dies as terror investigation examines nine deaths

world.title: Trump says Iran strikes unlikely if nuclear and Hormuz talks advance
world.summary: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 8 that renewed U.S. strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations produce a strong agreement on Tehran’s nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while warning that U.S. forces remain ready to attack. He said the military had identified 38 bridges as potential tar
world.content: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 8 that renewed U.S. strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations produce a strong agreement on Tehran’s nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while warning that U.S. forces remain ready to attack. He said the military had identified 38 bridges as potential targets. The conflict, now in its ninth month, remains at a stalemate, with shipping incidents continuing around the strait. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was not close to a diplomatic breakthrough and called Iran’s demands unacceptable. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said mediators had stopped traveling after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. He reiterated Tehran’s offer to reopen the strait within two days if Washington meets its conditions, including ending the war on all fronts. U.S. Central Command has established a roughly 20-person task force to disrupt routes carrying weapons and sanctioned goods across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea, expanding U.S. efforts beyond its naval blockade. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s prime minister on Monday, Nov. 9, as Doha continues mediation.
world.image_alt: Trump says Iran strikes unlikely if nuclear and Hormuz talks advance

business.title: Japan discloses record $50 billion day of yen buying as currency weakens
business.summary: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion ($50.4 billion) buying yen on July 30, part of three interventions totaling ¥15.4 trillion between July 30 and Aug. 3, Finance Ministry data released Monday showed. Japan coordinated the July 31 operation with the United States, the first joint yen-support action in nearly three deca
business.content: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion ($50.4 billion) buying yen on July 30, part of three interventions totaling ¥15.4 trillion between July 30 and Aug. 3, Finance Ministry data released Monday showed. Japan coordinated the July 31 operation with the United States, the first joint yen-support action in nearly three decades. The interventions briefly lifted the yen from a late-July low near 163 per dollar, but the currency later weakened to around 157-158, where it has traded for more than a month. Nikkei Asia cited structural obstacles to a sustained rise, while Kyodo said the persistent interest-rate gap between Japan and the United States continued to weigh on the yen.
business.image_alt: Japan discloses record $50 billion day of yen buying as currency weakens

business.title: Strong US jobs data props up dollar as markets await inflation
business.summary: The U.S. dollar held near a 1½-year high against the euro on Monday after October payrolls rose by 165,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1%, strengthening bets on a Federal Reserve rate increase in December. The dollar index traded around 102.2 after its biggest one-day rise in nearly six months on Friday. Markets put the
business.content: The U.S. dollar held near a 1½-year high against the euro on Monday after October payrolls rose by 165,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1%, strengthening bets on a Federal Reserve rate increase in December. The dollar index traded around 102.2 after its biggest one-day rise in nearly six months on Friday. Markets put the chance of a quarter-point hike at about 79%, with U.S. consumer-price data due Tuesday, Nov. 10. Asian currencies rose modestly as investors awaited the inflation figures. China’s October data showed faster producer-price inflation but slower consumer-price growth, while the Japanese yen drew support from Bank of Japan signals that further rate increases may be appropriate.
business.image_alt: Strong US jobs data props up dollar as markets await inflation

business.title: IRS raises 2027 tax brackets and child credit limits
business.summary: The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income tax bracket thresholds for 2027, allowing taxpayers to earn more before entering a higher bracket. Tax rates remain unchanged, with the top rate still 37%. For single filers, the 22% bracket starts above $52,025 and the 37% bracket above $661,375; for married couples f
business.content: The Internal Revenue Service raised federal income tax bracket thresholds for 2027, allowing taxpayers to earn more before entering a higher bracket. Tax rates remain unchanged, with the top rate still 37%. For single filers, the 22% bracket starts above $52,025 and the 37% bracket above $661,375; for married couples filing jointly, those thresholds are $104,050 and $793,650. The IRS also increased the maximum child tax credit to $2,300, including a refundable portion of up to $1,800, and raised the maximum earned income tax credit for qualifying families with at least three children to $8,496. The annual inflation adjustments are intended to keep wage increases from pushing taxpayers into higher brackets when their purchasing power has not increased.
business.image_alt: IRS raises 2027 tax brackets and child credit limits

business.title: NASA opens $10 billion lunar delivery framework to eight aerospace firms
business.summary: NASA on Nov. 7 made eight aerospace companies, including SpaceX and Blue Origin, eligible to compete for lunar delivery orders under a 10-year framework capped at $10 billion. The cap does not represent money already awarded: NASA will issue individual task orders for commercial companies to deliver scientific equipmen
business.content: NASA on Nov. 7 made eight aerospace companies, including SpaceX and Blue Origin, eligible to compete for lunar delivery orders under a 10-year framework capped at $10 billion. The cap does not represent money already awarded: NASA will issue individual task orders for commercial companies to deliver scientific equipment and infrastructure to support plans for a sustained presence near the Moon’s south pole. Separately, Blue Origin won a $94 million base contract to deliver NASA’s nuclear-powered PROMISE rover, with another $140 million available under an option. NASA is targeting a late-2028 launch for the 18-month mission. NASA also raised the maximum value of its existing lunar payload contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion.
business.image_alt: NASA opens $10 billion lunar delivery framework to eight aerospace firms

business.title: Democratic midterm gains put Trump-linked crypto firms under scrutiny
business.summary: Democrats’ victory in the U.S. midterm elections leaves crypto companies with ties to President Donald Trump facing potential congressional investigations when the new Congress convenes in January. The industry had backed Trump’s deregulatory agenda, but Democrats have said they will examine his family’s crypto busines
business.content: Democrats’ victory in the U.S. midterm elections leaves crypto companies with ties to President Donald Trump facing potential congressional investigations when the new Congress convenes in January. The industry had backed Trump’s deregulatory agenda, but Democrats have said they will examine his family’s crypto businesses and potential benefits to firms that supported his initiatives. The crypto sector spent nearly $200 million on the midterms through political groups, but many candidates it backed lost. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, the Connecticut Democrat expected to lead the Senate investigations subcommittee, has asked companies including World Liberty Financial, Binance and Tether, as well as donors to a White House ballroom project, to begin responding to records requests by Nov. 30. His letter warned that failure to produce the requested records by Jan. 4, 2027, could prompt other measures to compel compliance. The election also makes passage of crypto legislation less certain after the Senate failed in September to advance the Clarity Act, which would have established clearer rules for cryptocurrency exchanges and other digital-asset businesses.
business.image_alt: Democratic midterm gains put Trump-linked crypto firms under scrutiny

business.title: Asian stocks rebound after AI rout as Taiwan jumps 6%
business.summary: Asian stocks rose Monday, Nov. 9, after a week of steep losses linked to artificial intelligence: MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan gained 2%, Japan’s Nikkei rose 3.5% and Taiwan’s benchmark climbed more than 6%, according to Reuters. The gains followed Friday’s Wall Street recovery. Investors remain concerned
business.content: Asian stocks rose Monday, Nov. 9, after a week of steep losses linked to artificial intelligence: MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan gained 2%, Japan’s Nikkei rose 3.5% and Taiwan’s benchmark climbed more than 6%, according to Reuters. The gains followed Friday’s Wall Street recovery. Investors remain concerned that AI companies may struggle to earn returns on costly data-center investments and that Democratic gains in U.S. midterm elections could bring tougher rules for AI and data centers. CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco Systems are scheduled to report earnings this week, and U.S. consumer-price data is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. A report showing U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October—more than twice economists’ expectations—pushed market-implied odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least a quarter-point in December to nearly 80%.
business.image_alt: Asian stocks rebound after AI rout as Taiwan jumps 6%

business.title: Social Security retirement trust fund projected to exhaust reserves in 2032
business.summary: If Congress does not change Social Security financing, the retirement trust fund is projected to exhaust its reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032, leaving incoming revenue to cover about 78% of scheduled benefits and reducing payments by 22%. For a hypothetical single worker with career-average earnings of $34,000, t
business.content: If Congress does not change Social Security financing, the retirement trust fund is projected to exhaust its reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032, leaving incoming revenue to cover about 78% of scheduled benefits and reducing payments by 22%. For a hypothetical single worker with career-average earnings of $34,000, the monthly benefit at age 67 would fall from $1,543 to $1,204 after depletion; a middle-income couple’s combined benefit would fall from $5,096 to $3,975. Women’s average retired-worker benefit was $1,872.43 a month in December 2025, $409.85 below men’s, a gap attributed to earnings histories and time in paid work. In 2026, retirees who claim before full retirement age and keep working can have benefits withheld once earnings exceed $24,480. Social Security later recalculates payments at full retirement age, while claiming early permanently lowers the benefit.
business.image_alt: Social Security retirement trust fund projected to exhaust reserves in 2032

business.title: Wall Street futures rise as traders await inflation data, AI earnings
business.summary: U.S. stock futures rose Monday as investors awaited inflation data and earnings from artificial intelligence companies. The S&P 500 lost about 2.7% last week and the Nasdaq Composite fell 3.4%, despite a Friday recovery. CoreWeave reports Tuesday, Applied Materials on Thursday and Nvidia on Nov. 17; the consumer price
business.content: U.S. stock futures rose Monday as investors awaited inflation data and earnings from artificial intelligence companies. The S&P 500 lost about 2.7% last week and the Nasdaq Composite fell 3.4%, despite a Friday recovery. CoreWeave reports Tuesday, Applied Materials on Thursday and Nvidia on Nov. 17; the consumer price index is also due Tuesday, with producer prices scheduled for Friday. Investors remain concerned about strong jobs data and potentially tighter rules for data-center construction, energy use and development costs. Nvidia also faces a board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy, according to CNBC.
business.image_alt: Wall Street futures rise as traders await inflation data, AI earnings

science.title: Tencent scientist says AI could speed biological research and enable harm
science.summary: AI could help researchers discover drugs and conduct complex biological experiments but also pose risks if misused, Tencent chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu said at a science symposium in Hong Kong on Nov. 7. Yao said biological applications may be harder to manage than cybersecurity because beneficial and harmful uses ar
science.content: AI could help researchers discover drugs and conduct complex biological experiments but also pose risks if misused, Tencent chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu said at a science symposium in Hong Kong on Nov. 7. Yao said biological applications may be harder to manage than cybersecurity because beneficial and harmful uses are difficult to separate. Tencent is exploring autonomous laboratories in which AI would carry out experiments from start to finish, including work involving protein folding. A safety report drafted by Chinese technology companies including Tencent, Huawei and Alibaba also warned that AI’s improving performance on tasks such as pathogen design could pose public health risks.
science.image_alt: Tencent scientist says AI could speed biological research and enable harm

science.title: Climate change shifts Arctic greenery, darkens lakes and bleaches coral
science.summary: Climate change is altering natural colors across Arctic landscapes, lakes and coral reefs, with shifts linked to warming, permafrost thaw and pollution. A satellite study published in 2020 found greening at about 38% of sampled Arctic sites between 1985 and 2016. Another study found that green-wavelength values in more
science.content: Climate change is altering natural colors across Arctic landscapes, lakes and coral reefs, with shifts linked to warming, permafrost thaw and pollution. A satellite study published in 2020 found greening at about 38% of sampled Arctic sites between 1985 and 2016. Another study found that green-wavelength values in more than 400,000 North American boreal-Arctic lakes fell 15% between 1984 and 2019, indicating darker water. Darker lakes can retain heat longer, while coral bleaching leaves reefs more vulnerable to disease and other stressors. Researchers say thawing permafrost may be darkening lakes as soil mixes into the water.
science.image_alt: Climate change shifts Arctic greenery, darkens lakes and bleaches coral

science.title: NASA
science.summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory reentered Earth’s atmosphere and burned up over North Sumatra on Nov. 4, ending a nearly 22-year mission. Its observations, including millions of images, remain available for research. A 24-hour ultraviolet exposure of the Andromeda galaxy was assembled from observations made betwe
science.content: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory reentered Earth’s atmosphere and burned up over North Sumatra on Nov. 4, ending a nearly 22-year mission. Its observations, including millions of images, remain available for research. A 24-hour ultraviolet exposure of the Andromeda galaxy was assembled from observations made between May and July 2008. NASA said Swift detected about 20,000 ultraviolet sources there, many of them hot stars and star clusters obscured in visible-light views. Swift was designed to turn rapidly toward short-lived cosmic explosions and observe them in optical, ultraviolet and X-ray light. It also alerted other observatories so they could follow events before they faded. The U.S. Space Force said Swift reentered the atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST over North Sumatra. NASA expected most of the spacecraft to burn up, though some pieces may have survived.

science.title: Researchers map freshwater threats as newly identified Amazon fish faces extinction risk
science.summary: A global analysis mapped threats to more than 2,100 freshwater species, identifying agriculture and aquaculture as the leading pressure worldwide, followed by pollution and biological resource use. The researchers say the dominant threats vary by region, requiring conservation plans that target local pressures rather t
science.content: A global analysis mapped threats to more than 2,100 freshwater species, identifying agriculture and aquaculture as the leading pressure worldwide, followed by pollution and biological resource use. The researchers say the dominant threats vary by region, requiring conservation plans that target local pressures rather than a single approach everywhere. A separate study describes a newly identified Amazon killifish, *Laimosemion laranja*, found in three small forest pools near Laranjal do Jari, Brazil. Its known range covers about 25 square kilometers, and it faces threats from mining, deforestation, pollution and development. Researchers say it may meet International Union for Conservation of Nature criteria for Endangered status and recommend expanding a nearby reserve to include its habitat.
science.image_alt: Researchers map freshwater threats as newly identified Amazon fish faces extinction risk

science.title: Hazel dormouse numbers may have risen nearly 10% after years of decline
science.summary: Hazel dormouse numbers in England and Wales may have risen almost 10% between 2020 and 2025, after falling nearly 60% since 2000, according to monitoring data from the National Dormouse Monitoring Programme. Researchers say the estimate carries considerable uncertainty. The apparent increase coincided with warmer, drie
science.content: Hazel dormouse numbers in England and Wales may have risen almost 10% between 2020 and 2025, after falling nearly 60% since 2000, according to monitoring data from the National Dormouse Monitoring Programme. Researchers say the estimate carries considerable uncertainty. The apparent increase coincided with warmer, drier-than-average springs and summers. Scientists think warmer summers may reduce the time dormice spend in torpor, leaving them more time and energy to feed and breed. Conservationists say habitat protection remains essential; researchers also call for more study of climate effects, including how the animals may respond to warmer, wetter winters.
science.image_alt: Hazel dormouse numbers may have risen nearly 10% after years of decline

science.title: Studies link childhood fitness and later first sex to lower depression risk
science.summary: Two studies link early-life factors to depression in adulthood: an Australian cohort study found that higher aerobic fitness in childhood was associated with lower depression risk by middle age, while a separate study linked an older age at first sex to lower adult depression risk. The fitness link was more evident amo
science.content: Two studies link early-life factors to depression in adulthood: an Australian cohort study found that higher aerobic fitness in childhood was associated with lower depression risk by middle age, while a separate study linked an older age at first sex to lower adult depression risk. The fitness link was more evident among women. In the second study, education and household income explained much of the association. Neither study establishes that either factor itself prevents depression. The fitness study followed participants for an average of 32.5 years after tests conducted in 1985. The other study combined U.S. survey data with genetic analyses, which also identified education and income as important pathways. The researchers cautioned that genetic markers may reflect broader behavioral or socioeconomic tendencies.
science.image_alt: Studies link childhood fitness and later first sex to lower depression risk

science.title: NASA identifies Tennessee fireball as asteroid fragment; Hawaii fireball remains unidentified
science.summary: NASA said a fireball seen over southeastern Tennessee on Thursday was a roughly 2-inch, 6-ounce asteroid fragment that broke apart 25 miles above East Ridge after traveling at about 47,000 mph. Four NASA cameras recorded the fireball, which the agency said was not part of the Taurid meteor shower. A separate fireball s
science.content: NASA said a fireball seen over southeastern Tennessee on Thursday was a roughly 2-inch, 6-ounce asteroid fragment that broke apart 25 miles above East Ridge after traveling at about 47,000 mph. Four NASA cameras recorded the fireball, which the agency said was not part of the Taurid meteor shower. A separate fireball seen across Hawaii on Saturday remains unidentified. Astronomers at the W. M. Keck Observatory said its slower apparent movement and breakup were more consistent with a satellite or space debris re-entering Earth’s atmosphere than with a meteor, but they have not confirmed its identity.
science.image_alt: NASA identifies Tennessee fireball as asteroid fragment; Hawaii fireball remains unidentified

science.title: Diwali fireworks push New Delhi PM2.5 to nearly 59 times WHO limit
science.summary: New Delhi recorded an early-morning PM2.5 concentration of 879 micrograms per cubic metre in the Mandir Marg area on Monday, nearly 59 times the World Health Organization’s recommended daily maximum, after Diwali fireworks filled the city with smoke. Air quality exceeded the “severe” threshold in several parts of the c
science.content: New Delhi recorded an early-morning PM2.5 concentration of 879 micrograms per cubic metre in the Mandir Marg area on Monday, nearly 59 times the World Health Organization’s recommended daily maximum, after Diwali fireworks filled the city with smoke. Air quality exceeded the “severe” threshold in several parts of the capital, home to more than 30 million people. Firecrackers added to the winter pollution build-up from vehicle emissions, crop-residue burning and industry. Cool, still conditions can prevent pollutants from dispersing. Authorities had imposed traffic and construction curbs in recent weeks; on Friday, Delhi’s pollution action plan also called for schools to offer online classes.
science.image_alt: Diwali fireworks push New Delhi PM2.5 to nearly 59 times WHO limit

sports.title: Celtic beat Kilmarnock to preserve four-point Scottish Premiership lead
sports.summary: Celtic beat bottom-placed Kilmarnock 1-0 at Celtic Park on Sunday, with defender Liam Scales scoring the winner in the 26th minute. The result restored Celtic’s four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership after Rangers reduced the gap with a win on Saturday. An early goal by Kasper Høgh was ruled out, and Ki
sports.content: Celtic beat bottom-placed Kilmarnock 1-0 at Celtic Park on Sunday, with defender Liam Scales scoring the winner in the 26th minute. The result restored Celtic’s four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership after Rangers reduced the gap with a win on Saturday. An early goal by Kasper Høgh was ruled out, and Kilmarnock goalkeeper Nico Mantl saved Benjamin Nygren’s second-half penalty. The champions enter the international break with back-to-back wins after beating Besiktas 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday. Celtic manager Martin O’Neill said the packed midweek-and-weekend schedule had been tough, while Kilmarnock manager Neil McCann said his team had done enough to earn a point. Kilmarnock remain bottom of the table and winless in four matches.
sports.image_alt: Celtic beat Kilmarnock to preserve four-point Scottish Premiership lead

sports.title: Colts keep Daniel Jones despite calls before NFL trade deadline
sports.summary: The Indianapolis Colts, an NFL team, told quarterback Daniel Jones they will not trade him before Tuesday’s deadline, despite inquiries from other teams. Indianapolis fell to 2-7 after a 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, its fifth straight defeat. Jones threw for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception.
sports.content: The Indianapolis Colts, an NFL team, told quarterback Daniel Jones they will not trade him before Tuesday’s deadline, despite inquiries from other teams. Indianapolis fell to 2-7 after a 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, its fifth straight defeat. Jones threw for 180 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The Colts have traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. Jones has thrown six touchdown passes and 10 interceptions this season. His two-year, $88 million contract includes $38 million due in 2027, of which about $10.5 million is guaranteed against injury. The trade deadline is Tuesday; running back Jonathan Taylor and other Colts remain possible trade targets.
sports.image_alt: Colts keep Daniel Jones despite calls before NFL trade deadline

sports.title: Fermín López double gives Barcelona win over Atlético, extends lead at top
sports.summary: Barcelona came from behind to beat Atlético Madrid 2-1 in Madrid on Sunday, with midfielder Fermín López scoring twice to keep the Spanish champions top of La Liga. sports.content: Barcelona came from behind to beat Atlético Madrid 2-1 in Madrid on Sunday, with midfielder Fermín López scoring twice to keep the Spanish champions top of La Liga. Giuliano Simeone put Atlético ahead in the 10th minute; López equalised just before half-time and scored the winner in the 66th minute after a pass from Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal. The win left Barcelona on 33 points after 12 matches, three ahead of Real Madrid and five ahead of third-placed Atlético. It followed defeats by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in the preceding fortnight and ended Atlético’s seven-match league winning run. Barcelona will take that lead into the November international break. Their next league match is away to Villarreal on November 22; Atlético also return that day, away to Getafe.

sports.content: Brighton beat Brentford 2-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday to move into second place in the Premier League, five points behind leaders Arsenal. Diego Gomez opened the scoring in the 15th minute with a long-range strike, and Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross converted a penalty just before half-time. Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off in the 23rd minute after a video review of an incident in which he struck Brighton midfielder Chema Andres with his arm. Brighton have won seven of their first 10 league games, including victories over Arsenal and Manchester City. Sunday's victory followed five consecutive away fixtures, including a 1-0 win at Getafe on Thursday and the club’s first league victory at Manchester City the previous weekend. Brighton head into the November international break second, while Brentford are eighth with 14 points. Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler said his team must keep working on consistency rather than dwell on the table. The league resumes after the break.

sports.content: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Washington Commanders 20-13 on Sunday, but star receiver Puka Nacua injured his knee on the team’s final offensive play and is scheduled for an MRI on Monday, Nov. 9. The Rams’ initial assessment is that he did not tear his ACL; the scan will help determine the nature of the injury and whether he can play in upcoming games. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown that put the Rams ahead, while edge rusher Myles Garrett returned from a seven-game absence to record three sacks and force a fumble. Los Angeles won its third straight game to improve to 5-4. The Rams are already without receiver Davante Adams, who is on injured reserve, and visit Arizona next Sunday.

sports.title: Mahomes MRI shows no major elbow damage after Chiefs beat Jets
sports.summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ postgame MRI showed no major damage to his right elbow after he was hit while throwing in Sunday’s 35-12 win over the New York Jets. The test indicated an elbow strain or sprain. The team planned to monitor his elbow for pain and swelling, and Mahomes said he would prepar
sports.content: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ postgame MRI showed no major damage to his right elbow after he was hit while throwing in Sunday’s 35-12 win over the New York Jets. The test indicated an elbow strain or sprain. The team planned to monitor his elbow for pain and swelling, and Mahomes said he would prepare for next week’s game. Mahomes returned after the second-quarter hit and finished 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns. Running back Kenneth Walker III scored three times and gained 143 yards from scrimmage as Kansas City pulled away in the second half. The Chiefs’ defense held New York to minus-nine yards in the third quarter and sacked Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times. The victory ended Kansas City’s two-game losing streak and improved its record to 6-2; the Jets fell to 2-7 after a fourth straight loss. The Chiefs are scheduled to visit the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 15.

sports.title: Alcaraz beats Shelton to claim first Paris Masters title

sports.content: Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz beat American Ben Shelton 7-6(5), 7-5 on Sunday to win his first Paris Masters title, his ninth ATP Masters 1000 title and fifth trophy of 2026. Alcaraz, who had lost to Shelton in a five-set US Open quarter-final two months earlier, won in one hour and 57 minutes. After missing more than four months with a wrist problem, Alcaraz has won nine consecutive matches and three titles since returning at the US Open. In Paris, he saved four break points in the first set of the final, then recovered from a break down in the second. He had also saved two match points against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals. Alcaraz will next compete at the ATP Finals in Turin, scheduled for November 15-22, seeking his first title at the season-ending event. Shelton also qualified for the eight-player field, where the two could meet again.

sports.summary: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 at the Stadium of Light on Sunday, with Enzo Le Fée converting a 36th-minute penalty after striker Brian Brobbey went down under a challenge from defender Levi Colwill. sports.content: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 at the Stadium of Light on Sunday, with Enzo Le Fée converting a 36th-minute penalty after striker Brian Brobbey went down under a challenge from defender Levi Colwill. Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka went off injured before the fourth minute, but the hosts held on for their first league win since August. Chelsea had 68.7% possession but struggled to create clear chances. Their goalkeeper, Mike Penders, kept the deficit to one with a late save from substitute Wilson Isidor. The win lifted Sunderland off the bottom of the table, though they remained in the relegation zone. Chelsea fell to fifth with 16 points and four league defeats after 10 matches. The result ended Sunderland’s seven-match league winless run under head coach Régis Le Bris. Chelsea enter the November international break outside the top four. Sunderland visit Aston Villa and Chelsea host Leeds United on November 21.
